item.title: ServiceNow CVE-2026-6875 Exploited; 7-Zip CVE-2026-14266 and Gemini CLI Botnet Reported
item.content:encoded:
Critical ServiceNow code execution flaw now exploited in attacks — Must Read

Attackers are now exploiting CVE-2026-6875, a critical pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in the ServiceNow AI Platform, just days after patches were released. ServiceNow customers with self-hosted instances should upgrade to a fixed release immediately.

  • Threat intelligence company Defused says attackers have begun exploiting CVE-2026-6875, a critical vulnerability in the ServiceNow AI Platform.
  • Searchlight Cyber found and reported the vulnerability on April 1st, saying it can allow unauthenticated attackers to escape the sandbox and remotely execute code within the ServiceNow platform in high-complexity attacks.
  • ServiceNow addressed the flaw across hosted instances and released security updates for self-hosted instances on July 13th.
  • Defused observed the first in-the-wild exploitation attempts on Friday, days after ServiceNow issued patches.
  • ServiceNow’s official advisory still states that the company is not currently aware of exploitation against ServiceNow instances, while advising customers to upgrade to a patched release as soon as possible.

Russian-Speaking Hacker Uses Google Gemini CLI to Control Botnet of Eight Dental Clinic PCs — Should Read

Trend Micro found a Russian-speaking actor, “bandcampro,” using Google Gemini CLI as a hands-on hacking assistant to migrate and operate a small C2 botnet controlling eight dental clinic PCs. The case shows how AI agents can make criminal infrastructure fast to rebuild, easy to port, and usable by less-skilled operators despite safety guardrails.

  • Trend Micro analyzed 200 Gemini CLI session logs from March 19 to April 21, 2026, and found a Russian-speaking threat actor known as “bandcampro” using Google Gemini CLI for hacking activities.
  • The actor used Gemini CLI to deploy and operate command-and-control infrastructure that controlled eight computers in a dental clinic and accessed their OpenDental database.
  • Gemini CLI helped migrate the command-and-control server to a new virtual private server, configure Cloudflare tunnels, manage bots, and debug connectivity issues, with the migration completed in about six minutes.
  • The actor used the AI agent for botnet management tasks through natural language instructions in Russian, including checking active machines, sending file enumeration commands, and generating a one-line PowerShell infection command.
  • Trend Micro said the operation could be recreated from three plaintext markdown files totaling about 5 KB, making the infrastructure highly portable, disposable, and harder for takedowns to disrupt.

New 7-Zip Vulnerability Could Let Crafted XZ Archives Run Code During Extraction — Should Read

7-Zip has patched CVE-2026-14266, a high-severity heap buffer overflow in XZ archive handling that could allow code execution if a user opens a crafted archive. Users should manually update to 7-Zip 26.02 or later, as there is no evidence of public exploitation yet.

  • CVE-2026-14266 is a heap-based buffer overflow in 7-Zip’s handling of XZ chunked data that could allow code execution when a crafted XZ archive is opened.
  • 7-Zip fixed the flaw on June 25 in version 26.02, before Trend Micro’s Zero Day Initiative published details on July 15.
  • ZDI rated the vulnerability 7.0 High with a local attack vector, user interaction required, and high attack complexity.
  • As of July 20, 2026, The Hacker News found no public proof-of-concept and no credible reports of exploitation in the wild.
  • Users should manually update to 7-Zip 26.02 or later, and any product that ships a vulnerable copy of 7-Zip’s XZ decoder needs its own vendor fix.

Governing Agentic AI at the Decision Point: AWS + Netskope — Optional

The article argues that production agentic AI needs both deterministic tool-call authorization and semantic content inspection: AWS AgentCore Policy controls whether an agent may call a tool with specific parameters, while Netskope One AI Guardrails checks prompts and tool responses for injection, unsafe content, and data leakage.

  • Agentic AI deployments often harden prompts but spend little time securing what happens after the model decides to call a tool.
  • Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore evaluates every agent-to-tool request outside the agent’s code using default-deny Cedar policies where explicit forbids override permits.
  • The AWS policy engine can decide whether an agent may call a specific tool with specific parameters, but it does not reason about the meaning of prompt or response content.
  • Netskope One AI Guardrails inspects prompts and responses in real time for prompt injection, jailbreaks, harmful content, copyright or IP exposure, and tool-borne indirect injection.
  • The article argues that production agentic AI needs both AWS AgentCore policy controls for tool decisions and Netskope One AI Guardrails for content and intent inspection on every call.
